text:
Boston arrives having won its last two in extra time, 3-2 over Vegas in a shootout on Monday, and is 3-2-0 in its last five. Pittsburgh is coming off a 3-2 loss to the same Golden Knights, when Tomas Hertl scored with 0:35 left, and is winless in three (0-2-1). The Penguins are also without Bryan Rust, who is on injured reserve. Tommy Novak has moved onto Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell's line, up to 18:04 a night from 14:05. Evgeni Malkin is day-to-day. Connor Clifton also returns to Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving the Penguins.

The chance battle is close. Our model has Boston at 3.18 expected goals (the quality of chances) tonight and Pittsburgh at 3.06. At five on five, the Bruins have taken 52% of the expected goals in their games and the Penguins 53%. Boston draws a power play for the Penguins to chew on, taking 4.7 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Jeremy Swayman (+7.3 goals saved above expected, a measure of how many more shots he stopped than an average goalie would have) and Arturs Silovs (+1.8) both rate positively this season. Last year Swayman was +26.5 and Silovs -12.8.

Watch Pavel Zacha, 30% to score, and Crosby, also 30%. Rakell is on a four-game goal streak and sits at 31%. Our under-the-radar picks are Casey Mittelstadt, who has generated 2.5 expected goals in his last 10 games and is 21% to score, and JJ Peterka, 53% for a point with his ice time up.
